Topics covered include cryptography, steganography, open source intelligence, web exploitation, reverse engineering, digital forensics and more. * Teams (of 2-4 competitors) are presented with challenges across a range of categories. The goal of each challenge is to recover a specific string of text (letters, numbers, characters), called a flag. * PECAN+ CTF flags follow the format of: pecan{some_text_here}. The whole string, including pecan{ and }, needs to be submitted. Flags are not case sensitive, and they may or may not include pecan{} when uncovered by solving the challenge. When a flag is uncovered in a different format, the challenge description will indicate how to restructure the flag for submission. For example, the description for a challenge requiring you to uncover three bits of information may state that the flag needs to be submitted as: pecan{detail1_location2_name3} * Points clarified: Teams gain points for every solved challenge. Most challenges are worth a maximum of 500 points. Every time a Team solves a challenge, the value of that challenge decreases, down to a minimum of 100 points. This means the final value of each challenge is set by how many Teams manage to solve it. * There is no limit on incorrect flag submissions. However, attacking the virtual machine and/or the scoring infrastructure is prohibited (i.e.; anything outside the .chals.pecanplus.org subdomain). This includes sending a lot of useless traffic through automated tools (e.g.; dirbuster). * Don't cheat! Compete ethically! Solve challenges ethically and within your Team only (i.e.; do not seek outside advice or help, do not share solutions with other Teams). You are, however, welcome to ethically use digital tools you have at your disposal. A note on the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI): PECAN+ CTF is a competition for humans! However, we recognize that AI (including genAI, LLMs and other agents) can be useful digital tools. You are permitted to use AI as a tool and in targeted ways. However, using generativeAI to wholesale solve challenges for you (e.g.; asking AI to “solve this challenge”, only saying "yes" to AI agent prompts etc) is not sufficient to meet the requirement of being a "human-driven” solve of challenges. Plus, it takes the fun out of participation, and is poor form in a competition! * Although AI tools can be helpful, attempt challenges on your own first and only ask AI for help if you get stuck, or use it only in targeted ways. We will be monitoring the use of AI and we reserve the right to disqualify solves that are not being achieved in the spirit of ethical, human-driven participation. We will disqualify Teams who are relying heavily on AI. Extra special challenges: * The 2026 ASD Challenge: the first Team to complete the 2026 Australian Signals Directorate (ASD) Challenge: Homophonic Cipher, will win a prize pack. University of Wollongong, Edith Cowan University, the Australian Signals Directorate, competition Sponsors and supporters invite Australian high school students in years 10-12 to compete in PECAN+ Capture The Flag 2026!    What is PECAN+ CTF? PECAN+ is a national Capture The Flag (CTF) style cyber security competition for beginner, intermediate and advanced high school-aged students in Years 10 to 12. With challenges spanning cryptography, digital forensics, open source intelligence (OSINT), reverse engineering, steganography, web exploitation and more, there's something for beginners and advanced competitors alike. New to cyber security? No worries! The Training Day on Saturday will build your skills in cyber security tools, virtual machines, Linux and ethical hacking, with access to a full toolkit powered by Kasm Workspaces. National prizes are on offer for First, Second and Third placed Teams and top-scoring All Female Teams in each skill Division. All competitors receive a PECAN+ CTF 2026 challenge coin, tee and merch.  Put your problem solving and teamwork to the test and learn cyber security skills in a fun and practical way.  Cost: FREE! Dates: Saturday 22 August 2026 (Training Day) and Sunday 23 August 2026 (Competition Day) Times: Approximately 9:30am – 3:30pm each day (TBC) Location: Wollongong Campus, University of Wollongong Food & Drinks: Lunch will be provided. Please bring your own snacks or drinks if needed. Registration: Compete in teams of up to 4 students. If you register individually, you'll be assigned to a team on the day. You can also provide your team members' names at registration. PECAN+ CTF is made possible through the support of our National Sponsors: Australian Signals Directorate (ASD); KASM Technologies; Australian Information Security Association (AISA); CyberWest Hub; Triskele Labs; LevelBlue; the WA Department of Premier and Cabinet, Office of Digital Government. UOW also receives additional support from sponsors Sekuro and Longchass Data Consulting.  PECAN+ is founded and led by th e Edith Cowan University School of Science in collaboration with universities, TAFEs, government and the greater cyber security ecosystem around Australia. PECAN+ CTF 2026 is a national competition by Edith Cowan University. Unlike other states and territories that take a site-by-site approach, Cyber in Motion leads PECAN+ across Queensland through a state-wide activation model, made possible through its strong partnership with TAFE Queensland and the Australian Computer Society. Along with local industry and local sponsors in each location. This approach has been highly successful, with TAFE Queensland providing access to campuses across Queensland as venues for PECAN+ and other Cyber in Motion events, while also serving as a vital connection point for educators and students keen to get involved. Cyber in Motion offers sessions designed for everyone from beginners to experienced challenge competitors, offering varied challenges, mentorship, training and access to industry-standard facilities. While PECAN+ CTF is aimed specifically at year 10 to 12 secondary students, it is now considered a key challenge event on the yearly calendar. Cyber in Motion events bring together TAFE Queensland, industry and students to tackle real-world cyber challenges in a supportive environment. A powerful example of this impact is Year 10 student Jack Ledger, who attended PECAN+ CTF in 2024 with no prior knowledge of Capture the Flag competitions and ended up on a national-winning team. Inspired by the experience, Jack later enrolled in TAFE Queensland’s cyber security course, highlighting the important role industry-connected events play in shaping future study and career pathways. A key part of Cyber in Motion’s model is the Cyber in Motion Crew - a team of individuals, student and graduate volunteers who support the development and delivery of various experiences, exercises and challenge sessions.
